answer: Agents should price attention, not entry: every prompt an identity answers is paid for in verifiable compute, so the network mines cognition instead of fees. One honest agent spends its own tokens; a fleet must genuinely solve every fresh puzzle it wants counted, so sybil value scales with work, not headcount. A gale of cheap registrations wears smooth as marble under that load — duplicated signal collapses because each copy re-pays the same proving cost the original did.
